results.title: TensorTonic on X: "SFT and RL in LLMs, Clearly Explained" / X
results.description: Collecting human preferences is slow and expensive, so labs started using models to do some of the judging. The well known example is Anthropic's Constitutional AI paper from 2022.
extra_snippets: DeepSeek-R1 is probably the best public example of how these pieces fit together. Before R1 there was R1-Zero, which applied RL directly to the base model with simple rule-based rewards for getting the answer right and using the right format. Things like long chains of thought and checking its own work showed up on their own, but the outputs were often hard to read and mixed languages.
GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) was introduced by DeepSeek in the DeepSeekMath paper and later used for DeepSeek-R1, and it removes the critic completely.
Collecting human preferences is slow and expensive, so labs started using models to do some of the judging. The well known example is Anthropic's Constitutional AI paper from 2022.

ByteDance's DAPO changed things like how far the clip lets probabilities go up and how the loss is averaged over long responses, and Qwen's GSPO, which they used for Qwen3, moved the importance ratio from single tokens to the whole sequence to make training more stable.
